To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
5-substituents of indazoles are important for kinase inhibition.
5-substituents are important to kinase selectivity and that the 5-phenyl group can be used as a handle for further derivatization.
we have identified novel 5-subtituted indazole inhibitors of kinases such as Aurora2 and Jak 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and biological activity of novel 5-aryl and 5-amino indazoles as inhibitors for kinases.
the design, synthesis and evaluation of novel indazole derivatives as kinase inhibitors.
the development of new scaffolds for kinase inhibitor design and synthesis and the identification of novel kinase inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the indazoles are a promising class of scaffolds for the development of kinase inhibitors.
5-substituent indazoles are potent and selective kinase inhibitor scaffolds.
the 5-substituents are the most important structural feature for kinase inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel and efficient method for the synthesis of 5-subtituted indazoles, and that these compounds are potent inhibitors of kinases.
5-substituent indazoles and amines can be synthesized efficiently and in parallel fashion from readily available precursors employing [2+ 3] cyclo-additions.
the indazole core is a very promising core for kinase inhibitor design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
[2+3 cycloaddition] is a useful tool for the synthesis of novel scaffolds for kinase inhibitor discovery.
the indazole scaffold is a promising scaffold to target kinase enzymes.
the [2+3], [3+2], and [4+2] cycloadditon reactions are very useful in the design and synthesis of kinase inhibitors.
